originality.rationale: The direct motivating primary full text, including Theorem 3.1 and Appendix G Corollary G.3, establishes all-positive-moment divergence and only a non-sharp lower bound of form exp(-C log x/log log x). It does not identify the two-sided exact coefficient |log rho|. Zachary proves a general random-walk maximum theorem, but no identification of the Gaussian-refresh SGD stationary-error distribution or this block-increment scale. The separately examined regularly-varying-innovation result requires infinite-variance innovations and gives a distinct tail law. Targeted published-literature comparisons found no covering claim; unindexed equivalent regenerative-perpetuity specializations remain possible.

value.rationale: The motivating paper establishes infinite moments and Gaussian central probabilities but cannot quantify extreme failure frequency from those statements. The exact coefficient |log rho| resolves the mathematically natural missing upper/lower rare-error rate in a concrete stationary SGD example, distinguishing covariate persistence from learning-rate and noise-scale effects. It informs extreme-quantile risk assessment of algorithms under temporally persistent but marginally Gaussian designs; no broad practicality or full relative tail asymptotic is claimed.
